_doc: Hardware record: the class of every device the swarm uses (not exact models) and its typical real performance. Simulation parameters are derived from here (src/common/hardware.py); the launcher copies this file into config/swarm_runtime.json under 'hardware', where the simulator, drones and ship read it. Speeds and accelerations are scaled for the simulation by simulation.speed_scale; sensor noise, range and rate are used as they are. Classes marked simulated=false are recorded for hardware deployment but not modelled (their output is taken as perfect, or the device is unused).

simulation._speed_scale: sim speed = real speed x this; 0.1 reproduces the original 4 m/s drones; planned 0.2-0.4

uwb.class: IEEE 802.15.4z HRP UWB transceiver (DW3000-class), double-sided two-way ranging
uwb._rdl_payload: LOCALIZATION=rdl: 150 B per exchange (state 6 x float32, covariance 21 x float16, the one cross-covariance factor 36 x float16, header) plus a 26 B reply carried in a later frame; float16 left the simulated results unchanged. Needs 802.15.4z extended frames (DW3000-class: up to 1023 B); +112 B at 6.8 Mbps is ~0.16 ms per exchange, so the channel carries ~860 instead of 1000 exchanges/s.

uwb_anchors.class: ship-mounted UWB anchors (same transceiver class), positions in the ship frame

radar.class: 60 GHz FMCW mmWave radar (IWR6843AOP-class), four boards for 360 degree coverage

imu.class: MEMS 6-axis IMU on the flight controller (BMI088-class): the IMU a cheap drone already has, no custom unit
imu._accel_bias_mg: residual accelerometer bias after calibration, 1 sigma per axis; drifts in flight as a Gauss-Markov process with accel_bias_tau_s
imu._output_hz: the drone reads delta-velocity pre-integrated over each 50 Hz frame (the FIFO), not 400 Hz samples
imu._note: horizontal delta-velocity in the level frame (attitude from the AHRS entry) drives the EKF's prediction (NAV_PREDICT=imu). Error scaling follows the simulation's time stretch (hardware.imu_errors).

ahrs.class: flight-controller attitude estimate (gyro + accelerometer + magnetometer, complementary filter / EKF)
ahrs._note: attitude is otherwise taken as perfect; a tilt error leaks gravity into the horizontal axes, an equivalent accelerometer bias g*sin(tilt) (0.5 deg = 0.086 m/s^2, ~9x the accelerometer's own). Heading stays perfect (compass).

barometer.class: MEMS barometer (BMP390-class), fused with the IMU

compass.class: 3-axis magnetometer fused with the IMU (attitude/heading reference)
compass._note: heading taken as perfect; the attitude (tilt) error is modelled under ahrs

c2_radio.class: peer-to-peer data radio (Zenoh over UDP in the simulation)

environment.class: sea-state wind at drone altitude (not hardware: the conditions the hardware works in)
environment._note: real-world values, scaled by simulation.speed_scale like the airframe; a moderate breeze is ~5 m/s with ~1.5 m/s gusts. Default calm (0) keeps the original behaviour. Drones cannot sense it: it pushes their true position away from their dead-reckoned estimate.
